text: The electrode potential of $M^{2+}/M$ of 3d-series elements shows positive value for :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the electrode potential series, only copper have positive value for electrode potential because copper has lower tendency than hydrogen to form ions. $\therefore$ Electrode potential of Cu $E_{(Cu^{2+}/Cu)}^{o}$ show positive value.

text:
The product formed in the first step of the reaction of


[IMG]


with excess $\mathrm{Mg}/\mathrm{Et}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ ($\mathrm{Et}=\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}$) is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Magnesium inserts into a C-Br bond in dry ether to give an alkylmagnesium bromide: $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{Mg}{}^{\mathrm{Et}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}}\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{MgBr}$.

With excess Mg, both C-Br bonds of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Br})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Br})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ react, so the first-step product is the di-Grignard reagent $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{MgBr})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{MgBr})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

The dimers in (B) and (C) and 1-ethyl-2-methylcyclopropane in (D) require a further C-C coupling of an organomagnesium carbon with an unreacted C-Br bond, so none of them is the first-step product.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A proton and $a Li^{3+}$ nucleus are accelerated by the same potential. If $λ_{Li}$ and $λ_{p}$ denote the
de Broglie wavelengths of $Li^{3+}$ and proton respectively, then the value of
$\frac{λ_{Li}}{λ_{p}}$ is x $\times$ $10^{-1}$.

The value of x is $______. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[Mass of $Li^{3+} = 8.3$ mass of proton]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A particle of charge $q$ accelerated through a potential $V$ gains $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}=qV$, so

$λ=\dfrac{h}{mv}=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$

For the same $V$, $λ\propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{mq}}$. The proton has charge $e$; the $\mathrm{Li}{}^{3+}$ nucleus has charge $3e$ and mass $m_{\text{Li}}=8.3m_{p}$.

$\dfrac{λ_{\text{Li}}}{λ_{p}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_{p}\times e}{8.3m_{p}\times 3e}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{24.9}}=0.2004\approx 2\times 10^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
At 1990 K and 1 atm pressure, there are equal number of $Cl_{2}$ molecules and Cl atoms in the
reaction mixture. The value of $K_{p}$ for the reaction $Cl_{2 (g)}$ $⇌$ $2Cl_{(g)}$ under the above conditions
is x $\times$ $10^{-1}$.

The value of x is $_______. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Cl_{2}(g)$ $⇌$ 2Cl(g)

Let moles of both of $Cl_{2}$ and Cl molecule be x.

Partial pressure of Cl is, $p_{Cl}=\frac{x}{2x}\times 1=\frac{1}{2}$

Partial pressure of $Cl_{2}$ is, $p_{Cl_{2}}=\frac{x}{2x}\times 1=\frac{1}{2}$

Now, $K_{p}=\frac{(p_{Cl})^{2}}{p_{Cl2}}$

$\Rightarrow K_{p}=\frac{(1/2)^{2}}{1/2}=\frac{1}{2}=0.5$

= 5 $\times$ $10^{-1}$

Hence, x $\times$ $10^{-1}$

x = 5
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
When 9.45 g of CICH$_{2}$COOH is added to 500 mL of water, its freezing point drops by 0.5°C. The dissociation constant of CICH$_{2}$COOH is x $\times$ $10^{-3}$. 
The value of x is $________. ($Rounded
off to the nearest integer)

[$K_{f(H2}0) = 1.86 K kg$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{ClCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$ is $94.5\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so $n=\dfrac{9.45}{94.5}=0.1\text{mol}$ in $0.5\text{kg}$ of water and $m=0.2\text{mol kg}^{-1}$.

$\Delta T_{f}=iK_{f}m\Rightarrow 0.5=i\times 1.86\times 0.2\Rightarrow i=1.344$

For $\mathrm{ClCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}\mathrm{ClCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}+\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$, $i=1+α$, so $α=0.344$.

Taking $C\approx 0.2\text{mol L}^{-1}$ for this dilute solution,

$K_{a}=\dfrac{Cα^{2}}{1-α}=\dfrac{0.2\times (0.344)^{2}}{0.656}\approx 3.6\times 10^{-2}=36\times 10^{-3}$

Hence, the answer is 36.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
For the reaction $A_{(g)}$ $\to$ $B_{(g)}$ the value of the equilibrium constant at 300 K and 1 atm is equal to 100.0. The value of $\Delta_{r}$G for the reaction at 300 K and 1 atm in J mol$^{-1}$ is – xR, where x is $_______. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[R = 8.31 J mol$^{–1}K^{-1}$ and ln 10 = 2.3]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a reaction, A(g) $\to$ B(g)

Given, $K_{p} ($equilibrium constant) = 100

Temperature = 300 K

Pressure = 1 atm

Formula used, $\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$ $RT \ln  K_{p} .... (i)$

Here, $\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = standard Gibb's free energy

R = gas constant = 8.31 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$

Put value in Eq. (i), we get

$\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$ R (300) ln 100

$\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$ R (300) (2) ln (10)

$\because$ ln (10) = 2.3

$\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$ R(300) (2) (2.3)

$\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$ 1380 R

Hence, $\Delta$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$ xR

$\therefore$ x = 1380

text:
Gaseous cyclobutene isomerises to butadiene in a first order process which has a 'k' value of 3.3 $\times$ $10^{-4} s^{-1}$ at 153°C. The time in minutes it takes for the isomerization to proceed 40% to completion at this temperature is $______$.

(Rounded off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

It is a first order isomerisation reaction. Integrated rate law for 1st order reaction is

$kt=\ln \frac{[A]_{0}}{[A]_{t}}$ ...(i)

Here, 

k = rate constant

$[A]_{0}$ = initial concentration

$[A]_{t}$ = concentration at time 't'

Given, k = 3.3 $\times$ $10^{-4} s^{-1}$

$[A]_{0}=100\Rightarrow [A]_{t}=100-40=60$

Put values in Eq. (i), we get

$3.3\times 10^{-4}s^{-1}\times t=\ln \frac{100}{60}$

t = 1547.95 s = 25.79 min (1 min = 60 s or 1s = $\frac{1}{60}$ min) = 26 minutes
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift
